simple.meaning: קוֹרָה (qôwrâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a rafter (forming trenches as it were); by implication, a roof.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: קוֹרָה (H6982) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 19:8, with occurrences in Genesis, 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Song of Solomon.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קוֹרָה (H6982) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in קוֹרָה (H6982) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: קוֹרָה (qôwrâh) / H6982 is traced through Genesis 19:8, 2 Kings 6:2, 2 Kings 6:5, 2 Chronicles 3:7 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a rafter (forming trenches as it were); by implication, a roof
definitions.full: H6982. qorah קוֺרָה noun feminine rafter, beam (properly a thing meeting , fitting into, another); — suffix קֹרָתִי Gen 19:8 (J) = my roof-tree ; plural קֹרוֺת rafters , absolute 2Chr 3:7 , construct || 1Kin 6:15 b (reading ᵐ5 הַסִּמֻּן קוֺרוֺת Th Kit Benz, for קִירוֺת ᵑ0 ), + 7:7 b (reading הַקּוֺרוֺת for הַקַּרְקָ֑ע , see ׳ק ); Song 1:17 (|| רחיטנו Kt, רָהִיטֵנוּ Qr); more Gen beam , singular absolute קוֺרָה 2Kin 6:2 , 5 .

occurrences.englishText: See now, I have two virgin daughters. Please let me bring them out to you, and you may do to them what seems good to you. Only don’t do anything to these men, because they have come under the shadow of my roof.”
Please let us go to the Jordan, and each man take a beam from there, and let’s make us a place there, where we may live.”
But as one was cutting down a tree, the ax head fell into the water. Then he cried, and said, “Alas, my master! For it was borrowed.”
He also overlaid the house, the beams, the thresholds, its walls, and its doors with gold; and engraved cherubim on the walls.
